summary: This note covers the early life of Alexey Brodovitch, born in 1898 in Ogolichi, Russian Empire (now Belarus), into a wealthy family. His father was a physician, psychiatrist and huntsman, and his mother was an amateur painter. The family moved to Moscow during the Russo-Japanese War, and Alexey was sent to a prestigious school in Saint Petersburg, intending to enter the Imperial Art Academy.
one_line: Early life of Alexey Brodovitch, born 1898 in Ogolichi to a wealthy family, schooled in Saint Petersburg with art ambitions.
key_facts: Alexey Brodovitch was born in 1898 in Ogolichi, Russian Empire (now Belarus), to a wealthy family.
Brodovitch's father, Vyacheslav or Cheslau Brodovitch, was a respected physician, psychiatrist and huntsman.
Brodovitch's mother was an amateur painter.
During the Russo-Japanese War, the Brodovitch family moved to Moscow.
In Moscow, Brodovitch's father worked in a hospital for Japanese prisoners.
Alexey Brodovitch was sent to study at the Prince Tenisheff School, a prestigious institution in Saint Petersburg.
The intention was for Brodovitch to eventually enroll in the Imperial Art Academy.
Brodovitch had no formal training in art through his childhood.
As a child Brodovitch often sketched noble profiles in the audience at concerts in Saint Petersburg.
